stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine hold first US-led talks in nine months
body: Russia and Ukraine held US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi, their first in nine months.
US Secretary of State Rubio called them very productive; Zelenskyy called them constructive.
Three earlier rounds this year brought no big breakthrough.
stories.joke: Nine months between meetings: even dentists check in more often.
stories.vc: Real progress would cut energy prices and open a huge rebuilding market in Ukraine.

stories.headline: Indonesia's vice president offers to resign
body: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka offered to resign in a meeting with President Prabowo.
Questions are growing about whether he was eligible for the job.
It is not yet clear if Prabowo accepted.
stories.vc: Political turmoil at the top can unsettle investors in Southeast Asia's biggest economy.

stories.headline: Iran drops its 2,000 km limit on missile range
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they have lifted their self-imposed 2,000 km limit on ballistic missiles.
They did not say if Iran already has longer-range missiles.
Experts ask whether Iran now eyes targets beyond the Middle East.
stories.vc: Higher military risk keeps oil prices and Gulf shipping insurance elevated.

stories.headline: Bank stocks rise as markets pause after a big rally
body: The Nifty Bank jumped 1.5% on Monday, led by public sector lenders.
The Nifty closed up 0.23% at 25,045, and the Sensex up 0.13% at 81,107.
Analysts expect some profit-taking after a 10% rally in seven sessions.
stories.joke: Markets took a breather. Banks didn't get the memo.
stories.vc: Strong bank shares show investors expect loan growth to keep lifting profits.

stories.headline: Blackstone to buy 16% of IIFL Finance for $535 million
body: Blackstone will invest ₹5,000 crore for about 16% of lender IIFL Finance.
It is part of a ₹6,414 crore capital raise.
The money will lift IIFL's capital ratio to about 30% and fund gold loans.
stories.joke: Gold loans, now with Wall Street sparkle.
stories.vc: Big global funds buying into Indian lenders shows confidence in India's credit growth.

stories.headline: Three workers die from toxic gas at Tata's Hosur iPhone plant
body: Three contract workers died after allegedly inhaling toxic gas at Tata Electronics' iPhone factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.
They were cleaning a tank at the plant's effluent treatment unit.
The incident raises questions about worker safety in Apple's India supply chain.
stories.vc: Safety lapses can hurt Apple suppliers' push to scale up in India.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range, aiming for $1.4 trillion
body: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each.
That would raise up to $64 billion and value it at up to $1.404 trillion.
Each of its seven founders will sell shares worth about $250 million.
stories.vc: The biggest IPO ever would test how much public investors will pay for AI.

stories.headline: Oura buys AI primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
body: Smart-ring maker Oura is buying Counsel Health, which mixes AI chat with real doctors.
Counsel's service has been inside the Oura app since June.
The deal comes weeks after Oura shelved its IPO.
stories.joke: Your ring will now ask how you're feeling, professionally.
stories.vc: Wearable makers buying care services shows a push into paid health care.

stories.headline: X-energy wins approval to build its first small nuclear reactors
body: US regulators approved X-energy's permit to build four Xe-100 reactors at a Dow chemical plant in Texas.
Each makes 80 megawatts of power and 200 megawatts of heat.
It's the first such approval for an advanced reactor at a US industrial site.
stories.joke: Nuclear power, now available in a smaller size.
stories.vc: Small reactors could supply steady power for factories and AI data centres.

stories.headline: New York's AI safety law starts covering OpenAI and Anthropic
body: New York opened registration for big AI labs under its RAISE Act, due by 1 January 2027.
Labs with over $500 million revenue must publish safety plans and report serious incidents within 72 hours.
Fines can reach $1 million per violation.
stories.joke: Paperwork: the one thing AI can't skip.
stories.vc: State AI rules add compliance costs that investors will factor into AI lab valuations.

stories.headline: Google launches two new AI chips to challenge Nvidia
body: Google unveiled two new TPU chip systems, one for secure AI inference and one for memory-heavy AI agents.
TPUs are Google's custom chips for training and running AI models.
Google's TPU business now has nearly 100 customers.
stories.joke: Nvidia's monopoly now has a Google-shaped dent.
stories.vc: More chip competition could lower AI costs and pressure Nvidia's margins.

stories.headline: Bengal renames hospital harassment panels 'Abhaya Committees'
body: West Bengal will rename workplace harassment committees in its hospitals and medical colleges as 'Abhaya Committees'.
The name honours the doctor raped and murdered at RG Kar hospital.
The health minister ordered one set up at once at Kalyani's medical college.
stories.vc: Working complaint committees reduce legal risk and help hospitals keep women staff.

stories.headline: Defectors see Kim Jong Un's daughter as his likely heir
body: Many North Korean defectors believe Kim Jong Un's daughter, reportedly Kim Ju Ae, is being prepared as his heir.
State TV has often shown her beside her father.
She was last pictured with him at a military base in March.
stories.vc: A clear succession plan matters for regional stability and markets in East Asia.

stories.headline: Epstein survivor says her model agency put her in danger
body: A woman raped by Jeffrey Epstein says her model agency sent her to photoshoots at his Florida home.
She was 18 and had just arrived in the US from Uzbekistan.
She wants the agency held accountable.
stories.vc: Cases like this push agencies to adopt stronger safeguarding for young models.

stories.headline: MGM Medical College Indore gets 39 more specialist seats
body: MGM Medical College in Indore got approval for 39 more postgraduate seats across nine departments.
Its total PG seats rise to 322, the most in Madhya Pradesh.
It also offers 13 super-speciality seats.
stories.vc: More specialist trainees mean more doctors for government hospitals in central India.

stories.headline: Court orders fast hiring for Delhi's 1,000+ empty hospital jobs
body: The Delhi High Court told UPSC to start hiring for over 1,000 vacant doctor and staff posts in Delhi government hospitals.
It should not wait for the next yearly recruitment cycle, the court said.
Delhi must send revised hiring plans to UPSC within two weeks.
stories.vc: Staff shortages mean beds go unused; filling posts unlocks existing hospital capacity.

stories.headline: Bihar to hire over 11,000 staff for public health facilities
body: Bihar plans to hire more than 11,000 staff for its government health facilities.
The jobs cover medical support, technical, admin and clerical roles.
The official notice is expected in the last week of November.
stories.vc: Better-staffed public hospitals can treat more patients locally instead of sending them to Patna or Delhi.

stories.statLabel: races left: Vegas, Qatar, Abu Dhabi
stories.headline: F1 drops Imola backup and sticks with its Gulf finale
body: F1 will end 2026 with Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, dropping Imola as a backup finale.
The Iran war already cancelled Saudi Arabia and moved Bahrain's race to Malaysia.
F1 says safety comes first if the conflict escalates.
stories.vc: Keeping the Gulf races protects big hosting fees for F1's final weekends.
